title: Inspect pinned generated authentication before adapting it
outcome: An inspected generator baseline fixes the actual auth adaptation points before migrations or web consumers fork.
scope: Inspect the exact P0-generated code, generator version, routes, token format, timestamps, cookie options, scope and recent-authentication behavior.
Record concrete Accounts/session-row reference, family-topic and sudo integration points beside generated code/tests; identify which generated password paths must be absent.
acceptance: Evidence names actual generated files and defaults; 15-minute magic links, seven-day email-change links, 60-day sessions and seven-day renewal are explicit Tips adaptations.
A small executable inspection fixture establishes real reauthentication advances authenticated_at while renewal preserves it; no claim that the generator already supplies family semantics.
verification: Generator/version evidence and focused generated-auth baseline tests, with exact commands recorded after P0 chooses the app layout.
ownership: Generated Accounts/UserAuth code and focused auth inspection fixtures
sizing: One inspection/probe of the pinned generated auth baseline and adaptation points. Schema changes remain P1.02 and production auth behavior remains P2; do not implement the complete auth flow here.

title: Install identity and session-family schema
outcome: Users and generated tokens enforce the canonical identity, deletion and family invariants.
scope: Adapt generated users/users_tokens migration and Ecto schemas only; reserve migration order with the integration owner.
Named role/ban/deletion/handle/email checks, case-insensitive unique indexes, session-only UUID family constraint and family/token indexes.
acceptance: Reject invalid/reserved handles at the appropriate application boundary; DB rejects invalid shape, duplicate case variants, inconsistent deletion/null identities and ban/date pairs.
Session rows require a family and non-session rows reject one; token formats and generated timestamp semantics remain compatible.
Account physical deletion cascades tokens only; no cascade erases contributions.
verification: Fresh migration and rollback/reapply tests for identity tables; direct constraint rejection fixtures and generated auth schema tests.
ownership: Identity migration; Accounts user/token schemas; identity DB tests
sizing: One identity/token schema family with migration and rejection fixtures. No auth pages, renewal implementation or account lifecycle workflows.

title: Install contribution and curated-vocabulary schema
outcome: Tips and reviews have canonical validation, submission identities, versions, ranking columns and read indexes.
scope: Create models/environments/tags, tips/reviews, named checks, live views and non-search content indexes.
Implement epoch helper and generated Hot/Wilson expressions; represent stable setup fields and two independent visibility markers.

Provide idempotent development/test/M1 synthetic vocabulary fixtures or an explicit seed entry point, including Other technique and a minimal model/environment set. Clearly mark synthetic fixtures; production vocabulary remains owner-reviewed and no synthetic firsthand experience enters production.
acceptance: Enforce title 3–140, tip body 3–20000, review body 1–20000, prompt/output max20000, model_other max80 and selected/custom-model exclusivity, with whitespace rejection as specified.
Submission keys remain unique per author even after hide/delete; only one undeleted review per author/tip, including hidden reviews.
Hot divisor345600 and Wilson z1.281551565545 match fixtures; deleted/hidden rows leave public views; vocabulary has active/sort_order fields.
A fresh local or M1 test environment can render required technique choices without manual database edits; Other technique exists and repeated seed execution does not duplicate rows.
verification: Migration/reapply tests and direct invalid-row fixtures; generated ranking and live-view membership examples.
ownership: Content/vocabulary migration and schemas; schema constraint fixtures
sizing: One contribution persistence family, ranking definitions and minimal synthetic vocabulary fixtures. Do not implement publishing, vote triggers or search queries.

title: Install votes and authoritative counter triggers
outcome: Vote and live-review changes update counters exactly once under concurrent transactions.
scope: Create votes/checks/partial unique indexes and the two narrow OLD/NEW delta triggers.
App code never writes counters; preserve immutable vote targets and review parent ids at context boundaries.
acceptance: Vote insert, value change, identical update, removal and invalidation produce the correct up/down deltas for either target.
Review insert, hide, restore and delete adjust the parent count only for liveness transitions; text edits change no count.
Overlapping independently committed votes keep nonnegative correct counters; opposing review liveness/bulk lock schedules use actual FK/trigger targets.
verification: Database counter matrix and synchronized multi-connection concurrency tests on complete currently integrated schema, followed by recount comparison.
ownership: Vote migration/schema; counter functions/triggers; DB concurrency fixtures
sizing: One authoritative counter mechanism with focused vote/review transitions and synchronized database fixtures. Product voting and bulk moderation stay with their feature tasks.

title: Install report and notification persistence invariants
outcome: Reports and folded notifications provide the database keys required by later transactional operations.
scope: Create flags and notifications plus open-report, folding and read indexes; no workflow UI in this task.
Use named enums/checks for reason/type, one target, report detail and notification count/type-target compatibility.
acceptance: A reporter cannot create two open flags for the same target; resolution permits another flag on unchanged content.
Reason fabricated is accepted, wrong is rejected; detail above1000 is rejected.
Only one unread fold exists per recipient/type/target with NULLS NOT DISTINCT; read rows permit later unread folds; tip_reviewed points to a review.
verification: Direct insert/update constraint and partial-index conflict tests; migration rollback/reapply evidence.
ownership: Report/notification migration and schemas; focused DB tests
sizing: One persistence boundary for reports and folded notifications. No report workflow, inbox UI or full notification-operation implementation.

title: Install media identity and lifecycle schema
outcome: One media table represents images, staged/attached private videos and durable cleanup without ambiguous membership.
scope: Create media schema, checks, provider uniqueness, deferrable slots and static expiry index.
Declare typed upload target, canonical encoder ownership and media result fields for P5/P3 consumers; no provider calls.
acceptance: Reject invalid provider/kind/state combinations, ready duration outside(0,180], ready without trusted completion, mixed parents, image staging, and attached media with expiry.
Accept failed NULL-uid reservation, staged uploading video, attached ready video and cleanup row retaining provider/parent identity with NULL position.
Swapping positions succeeds when deferred; invalid duplicate/final slots or an eleventh slot fail. Expiry index contains no time-dependent predicate.
verification: Media lifecycle constraint matrix, deferred-order tests, migration inspection and rollback/reapply.
ownership: Media migration/schema; typed target declaration; lifecycle fixtures
sizing: One media persistence state model and identity contract. Provider calls, claim behavior and cleanup workers are separate P5 tasks.

title: Install extension-backed search schema
outcome: Search side tables and indexes run on the actual pinned extension-enabled database.
scope: Create tip_search/review_search with1024-dimensional vectors, freshness and cooldown columns, BM25/HNSW/pending indexes.
Declare Search-owned text-writer signature for caller transactions; keep content counter updates independent from search storage.
acceptance: Both extension index families create and work on the P0 image; incompatible versions block completion.
Wrong vector dimension fails; rows reference the intended content, and missing-vector indexes do not pretend to enforce parent visibility.
Migration down/up handles extension dependency order and preserves the request-pool timeout policy.
verification: Full extension migration log, actual BM25/vector index smoke queries and constraint tests; version evidence.
ownership: Search migrations/schemas; writer signature declaration; extension fixtures
sizing: One extension-backed search persistence family and writer signature. No retrieval tuning or embedding runtime implementation.

title: Define current-admission scope and operation outcomes
outcome: Consumers share one concrete Accounts admission interface instead of inventing token or ban checks.
scope: Define exact scope fields, private server session-row reference and result/error shapes beside Accounts code/tests.
Separate authenticated admission, confirmed contribution eligibility, moderator authority and own/account deletion capability during full ban.
acceptance: Representative controller, LiveView and worker caller examples establish who creates scope and who rechecks locked business eligibility.
Bearer tokens and row references are absent from public projections/events; client-provided scope/session identity is rejected.
Public reads require no token lookup; privileged reads and mutations use the common validity definition, including expiry/revocation.
verification: Contract examples/types and compilation tests against actual generated interfaces; consumer review by content/editor owners.
ownership: Accounts scope/admission declarations; contract fixtures
sizing: One Accounts scope/admission contract with representative caller shapes. Runtime admission is P2.05; avoid a parallel universal authorization framework.

title: Implement shared visibility policy and projection contracts
outcome: Every consumer has one tested visibility decision and narrow projection shapes that prevent hidden/deleted data leaks.
scope: Implement visibility policy for ordinary/author/moderator callers and narrow projection examples for summary, tip, review, metadata and media.
Declare capability, source-labelled excerpt and selected-review result shapes; P9/P4/P12 implement their own queries.
acceptance: Author deletion masks original text, title, slug, attribution and media for all viewers, including moderators.
Hidden content remains author/moderator-only, while an independently visible review survives a hidden/deleted tip with masked parent context.
Unknown/wrong-parent review ids disclose no data; raw structs/nested associations never bypass projection; moderation report details do not reach authors.
verification: Table-driven visibility/projection matrix including metadata, slugs and media references; representative consumer fixture compilation.
ownership: Content visibility policy and projection declarations; visibility fixtures
sizing: One shared visibility decision matrix with narrow projection contracts. Actual browse/profile/search queries belong to their consumers; split an unexpectedly large projection family before dispatch.

title: Fix whole-intent publication and edit boundary contracts
outcome: Editor, Media and Search owners can implement against exact input and receipt shapes without a second specification.
scope: Declare publishing/edit signatures, normalized whole-intent comparator ownership, ordered upload identities and created/equivalent/different/unknown receipts beside code/tests.
Define complete editable base, original expected version, no-op result and current capabilities; coordinate exact routes shared with P9a.
acceptance: Examples cover same key/different intent, missing file identity, hidden/deleted originals, no-op edit and stale version; identity alone never acknowledges draft values.
Context inputs contain files/ids and explicit values, never socket/upload entries; provider work stays outside DB locks.
Search-writer and notification participants are required within publication/edit transactions; declarations do not return successful stubs.
verification: Executable shape/normalization examples and cross-owner contract review; downstream issues link exact symbols before Ready.
ownership: Content boundary declarations and examples; shared editor/media/search contract fixtures
sizing: One publication/edit input-and-receipt contract with examples. P3 implements normalization and editor behavior; browser storage/event extensions must consume this contract.

title: Verify complete canonical schema and lock graph
outcome: The assembled schema, rather than historical reduced scripts, is a verified foundation for feature work.
scope: Run all integrated migrations from empty DB, rollback/reapply as supported and the actual release migration command on the pinned image.
Audit each canonical table/check/index/view/trigger and generated auth/Oban migration against the implemented schema; replay focused lock schedules.

This is a bounded verification gate over already integrated P1 migrations and fixtures, not a new schema or application implementation task. Run direct database schedules for existing constraint/trigger/FK behavior; defer complete application-operation races to their owning feature gates. Assign any required repair to its owning issue and keep this gate blocked until that reviewed repair is integrated.
acceptance: No canonical invariant or search extension is skipped; evidence lists actual versions, revision and test names.
Concurrent report insertion/deletion and review liveness/counter schedules include actual trigger/FK locks and deterministic synchronization.
Request statement timeout remains2s after maintenance/migration use; no generic deadlock retry hides ordering defects.
verification: Fresh database/release migration logs; schema coverage checklist; complete DB constraint suite and focused concurrency results.
ownership: Schema integration tests and coverage evidence; migration-order coordination
sizing: One verification session over the pre-existing schema coverage checklist and focused DB fixtures. Do not invent or implement missing auth/publication/moderation features in this gate. Missing fixtures or failed invariants return to their named P1 owner; retain this issue as the integration gate.

title: Implement one-form registration with stable handles
outcome: New contributors register an email and chosen handle together without accidental identity changes.
scope: Neutral-word/random-suffix suggestion, fixed-handle guidance, chosen-handle/email validation and case-insensitive constraint feedback.
Verify Turnstile before registration using P13a configuration; preserve allowed return destination and all input through failures.
Consume P16.02-owned shared component interfaces; reserve any required shared-file change through its owner instead of creating parallel controls.
acceptance: Suggestion/availability checks create no user or reservation; rerenders never overwrite an edited suggestion.
Concurrent handle claims return one winner and field feedback to the other; registered email offers sign-in without replacing identity.
Reserved handles admin/moderator/mod/staff/support/deleted/removed fail; account settings cannot rename handles; unverified accounts gain no contribution access.
verification: Accounts and signup form tests, concurrent uniqueness test, Turnstile success/failure contract tests; real configuration evidence joins auth gate.
ownership: Registration Accounts functions and signup page/controller; identity tests
sizing: One registration form and its account-creation behavior using existing scope, limiter and UI contracts. Expiry/reclaim, mail transport and cross-browser return are separate tasks.

title: Serialize registration verification, expiry and reclaim
outcome: Expired unconfirmed registrations release identities without deleting confirmed accounts or reviving old tokens.
scope: Use one guarded cleanup/reclaim path in signup and bounded maintenance; confirmation uses the same row-lock deadline rules.
Keep original inserted_at immutable and deadline seven days despite resend; token consumption and account state commit together.
acceptance: Confirmation versus cleanup/reclaim in both orders rechecks clock time after waits; a successful confirmation survives, late confirmation rejects even before scheduled cleanup.
Conflicts on different email/handle rows acquire account locks in id order; old tokens never authenticate replacement accounts.
Unexpected FK violation is an operational invariant error with preserved input, not normal uniqueness feedback or content cascade deletion.
verification: Clock-boundary and synchronized multi-connection confirmation/reclaim tests; maintenance batch bound evidence and old-token replacement-account test.
ownership: Accounts registration lifecycle; expiry maintenance worker; race fixtures
sizing: One shared seven-day registration deadline/cleanup/reclaim invariant. Keep confirmation races here; unrelated token renewal and account deletion remain separate.

title: Implement session-family creation and renewal
outcome: Browser sessions renew within a stable family using the existing generated token format and genuine-authentication recency.
scope: Fresh browser login creates a server UUID family; same-account renewal and reauthentication retain it.
Account lock precedes predecessor context/expiry/account revalidation; bounded pruning uses the common validity function.
acceptance: 60-day server/cookie validity and seven-day renewal work at boundaries; magic-link validity15minutes and email-change link validity7days remain distinct.
Concurrent renewal successors share one family; renewal copies authenticated_at and true reauthentication advances it.
Expired or wrong-account predecessor cannot create a successor; pruning an expired initial token leaves valid successors valid.
verification: Real cookie expiry/renewal tests, two-successor race and token-pruning/sudo-recency fixtures.
ownership: Accounts token/session functions; generated UserAuth adaptation; session tests
sizing: One session-family creation/renewal invariant including shared validity and bounded pruning. Logout and account switching remain P2.04.

title: Make family logout and account switching revoke admission
outcome: Logout cannot be undone by a late renewal response, and switching accounts revokes the old browser family.
scope: Logout takes account lock, deletes family in transaction, then broadcasts stable family topic.
Account switch locks old/new users in id order, validates login proof and starts the new account family; expose revocation helper for P12 email change/deletion.
acceptance: Both renewal/logout schedules and late cookies fail admission after revocation; another browser family remains valid.
Lost disconnect delivery cannot restore authorization; same-account reauthentication does not accidentally create an independent family.
Invalid switch proof leaves prior account state coherent; valid switch prevents old family from granting later privileged access.
verification: Synchronized session races, controller cookie tests and two-browser family isolation tests.
ownership: Accounts family revocation; UserAuth logout/switch paths; auth race tests
sizing: One family revocation boundary covering logout and browser account switching. Reuse session validity; email-change and account-deletion operations are P12 consumers.

title: Enforce fresh admission on privileged boundaries
outcome: Long-lived pages use current session/account state before every privileged operation.
scope: Adapt generated lookup once to return identity and token-row id; bind server-private reference to mounted account.
Expose reusable admission helper and wire existing auth surfaces; downstream feature tasks must use it for their own privileged reads/mutations.
acceptance: Expired/revoked token, deleted account, stale role and account switch reject privilege even if socket stays connected.
Unconfirmed/full-ban accounts cannot contribute; full bans preserve own-content/account deletion capabilities.
Public rendering does not query token state; workers use business eligibility rather than browser session; bearer/reference values do not render or leak to logs.
verification: Controller/LiveView admission matrix with failed disconnect, forged reference and changed role/ban fixtures; consumer contract tests.
ownership: Accounts admission helper; UserAuth hooks/plugs; scope fixtures
sizing: One reusable current-admission boundary with generated auth hooks/plugs. Each later feature wires its own privileged call sites using the proven contract.

title: Deliver bounded authentication mail with honest outcomes
outcome: Direct authentication email delivery preserves identity and gives honest retry feedback after the shared limiter admits a request.
scope: Use direct Swoosh delivery outside DB transactions after account/token persistence; configure a measured provider timeout.
Call the P2.09 limiter before token creation and mail delivery for sign-in, verification resend and email-change requests, including LiveView events. Do not implement a second limiter.
Preserve generated notifier/token contracts and safe return destinations; authentication mail never uses Oban or durable automatic retries.
acceptance: Provider rejection, timeout and uncertain acceptance preserve account/email identity and explain retry without claiming no message was sent.
No auth Oban jobs or automatic mail retry loop; repeated request follows limits and does not extend registration deadline.
Route/event equivalence and forged forwarded-IP tests prevent limiter bypass; disallowed requests create neither token nor mail.
verification: Req.Test/selected-adapter rejection, timeout and uncertain-delivery tests; verify limiter denial causes neither token creation nor a provider call. Record one redacted real staging mail result at P2.08.
ownership: Accounts notifier/auth mail request handlers; mail failure and limiter-integration tests
sizing: One authentication-mail transport boundary using the existing P2.09 limiter. No second rate limiter, email job queue or account lifecycle redesign.

title: Carry safe authentication return destinations across browsers
outcome: Completing an emailed link in another browser returns to the intended authorized destination without replaying an action.
scope: One allowlisted local return_to carrier spans sign-in/signup, link, confirmation and controller redirect; choose real router/live-session navigation.
Recheck target access after sign-in; reopen permitted report/editor interaction while preserving explicit user action requirements.
Consume P16.02-owned shared component interfaces; reserve any required shared-file change through its owner instead of creating parallel controls.
acceptance: Cross-browser confirmation works without original cookie; unsafe scheme/host/protocol-relative/encoded destinations fail closed to a safe route.
Public LiveView vote/report sign-in carries destination without writing Plug session; no vote/report/save/delete occurs automatically.
Unavailable target or account switch is handled honestly; no draft content or pending mutation is embedded in URL/email.
verification: Two-browser actual magic-link flow; malicious-return matrix and no-side-effect assertions for vote/report/editor destinations.
ownership: Auth return_to validation/carrier; routes/controllers; browser auth journey tests
sizing: One validated destination carrier across the auth journey. Reuse completed registration/session/mail components; no replay of product mutations.

title: Prove integrated identity and admission boundary
outcome: The early auth gate passes with real browser contexts and configured providers on one integrated revision.
scope: Run the complete identity boundary matrix, plus actual cross-browser verification and target return.
Record provider configuration, failed-delivery feedback, cookies, seven-day expiry lock waits and revocation evidence; feature-specific consumers are later gates.
acceptance: All auth tests pass with no P0/P1 findings and no mocked provider counted as real success.
Lost disconnect, late renewal cookie, independent browser and sudo-recency cases pass; credentials and magic tokens are absent from recorded evidence.

Exercise real configured Turnstile validation and direct mail acceptance in staging, including invalid challenge rejection; acceptance by the mail provider is not claimed as guaranteed inbox delivery.
verification: Integrated auth test report, redacted real-provider/browser journey record and independent commit/PR reviews.
ownership: Auth integration tests and early-gate evidence
sizing: One integrated authentication verification session over existing tests and real providers. Failed behavior returns to its owning issue; do not build missing auth features in the gate.

title: Implement reusable bounded ETS admission limits
outcome: Authentication, contribution and upload callers share one tested single-node limiter with explicit numeric budgets and trusted client identity.
scope: Implement one supervised ETS-backed limiter with an injectable clock and bounded retention; choose initial numeric auth, per-user write and upload limits with documented rationale.

Define exact caller API for normalized destination address plus trusted client IP on authentication requests, and server-admitted account identity on writes/uploads. Callers cannot select another account or trust arbitrary forwarded headers.
Test HTTP and LiveView caller metadata paths; deployment-specific proxy allowlisting is installed and tested by P13b.01. Expose a shared helper, not a second scheduler or separate service.
acceptance: Concurrent requests at each configured boundary admit only the intended budget; expired entries can be reclaimed without unbounded memory growth.
Normalized email case/whitespace and HTTP versus LiveView requests share the intended bucket; spoofed forwarded/client fields cannot create trusted identities.
Limit denial provides retry feedback before token creation, provider request or business mutation; deletion does not restore consumed contribution budget.
Server-authorized callers can use separate auth/write/upload policies through the same implementation; no dependency on registration or mail delivery is introduced.
verification: Clock-controlled concurrent ETS limiter tests, bucket normalization/identity-forgery cases and representative HTTP/LiveView metadata integration fixtures. Record numeric limits and bounds beside configuration.
ownership: Shared application limiter and supervision reservation; trusted request-identity helper; limiter fixtures
sizing: One reusable admission mechanism and its clock/identity contract; mail transport and each feature caller are separate tasks. Split deployment proxy configuration into P13b.01, not a new limiter.

title: Implement one transactional search-text writer
outcome: All future publication, searchable edit and retag callers share one atomic text/freshness/invalidation operation.
scope: Build normalized documents from tip title/body/prompt/output/tag and own model/environment labels or free text, and corresponding review fields.
Write search_text plus a fresh text_at, clear embedding and reset embed_after within the caller transaction; provide explicit label-rebuild path.
acceptance: Output-only changes and retag change freshness; vote/counter changes do not; caller rollback rolls back the search update.
Two successive changes have distinct freshness even inside a transaction; stale worker success and failure cannot overwrite the newer text.
Review setup is indexed independently without changing parent filter eligibility; no OCR/transcription and no second text builder.
verification: Builder field/normalization fixtures; transactional rollback and successive-freshness tests; consumer contract tests ready for P3.
ownership: Content.Search text builder/writer; focused search write tests
sizing: One normalized search-document writer and transactional freshness invariant. Retrieval, embedding jobs and authoring consumers remain separate tasks.

title: Define ten-query relevance gate and select embedding candidate
outcome: The search owner establishes an executable ten-query corpus and measurable pass rules before tuning or selecting a runtime.
scope: Use feature-specific credentials and nonsecret configuration from P13a.01 in an isolated probe using P0.02 dependencies. This probe does not require a deployed release or unrelated providers. Final integration uses P13a.02 runtime configuration at the feature gate.

Create labelled synthetic developer-task corpus and ten exact queries, expected relevant tips/reviews and evaluated rank cutoff, including scoped coding changes, setup, long outputs and punctuation/error messages.
Evaluate hosted1024-dimensional candidate first with its specified document/query preparation, numeric input/latency/recall limits, capacity and price at measured volume.
Record self-hosted Qwen fallback only if hosted gate fails or owner rejects off-box queries; pin one model/runtime and no mixed-vector policy.
acceptance: Gate thresholds and relevance judgments are explicit before comparison; no invented claim that all ten already pass.
Long input has a deterministic model-compatible handling rule with measured relevance/memory effects; reader queries and eligible public text only reach provider.
Provider credentials or runtime capacity absence leaves probe blocked; proposed material spending/privacy change goes to owner.
verification: Committed corpus/query labels, repeatable evaluation entry point, raw redacted model/latency/recall results and selected configuration or explicit blocker.
ownership: Search evaluation fixtures/probe; embedding provider configuration
sizing: One isolated ten-query/provider evaluation and runtime decision. Set explicit thresholds before comparison; full application retrieval is P4b.02 and integrated quality proof is P4b.07.

title: Implement pinned hybrid ranking and authorized hydration
outcome: Search returns a current authorized bounded ranking with correct lexical matches and exact parent-tip filters.
scope: Implement four branches, RRF constant60, branch top50 tip candidates, review pre-collapse top1000, one best matching review and fixed final200-tip window.
Put active tag/model/environment predicates in every branch; hydrate summaries/votes/capabilities/excerpts through policy and preserve rank order.
acceptance: Nonnegative lexical scores never gain rank under actual sequential/index plans; stopwords/zero/few matches and escaped quotes/error text behave as ordinary text.
Review model metadata cannot satisfy parent-tip model filter; hidden/deleted parent or review cannot leak excerpt/title/slug after candidate selection.
20-row final pages use validated offsets0–180 and tip-id tie-break; no branch-local offset or growing candidates; matching source labels Review/Prompt/Result/Reviewer setup are explicit.
Filtered HNSW iterative relaxed results are materialized/re-sorted and measured against exact recall expectations.
verification: Pinned SQL integration tests including EXPLAIN plans, visibility-change hydration test and filtered-recall corpus comparison.
ownership: Content.Search retrieval SQL and hydration; search DB integration tests
sizing: One bounded retrieval/hydration behavior on pinned SQL. Keep timing orchestration and LiveView out; split ranking versus hydration before dispatch if the concrete fixture/read set exceeds one session.

title: Implement bounded singleton embedding scan
outcome: Missing vectors progress fairly through one bounded durable scan without stale writes or per-row job growth.
scope: Periodic singleton active-state uniqueness, embeddings queue concurrency1/max_attempts1, up to50 alternating tip/review rows.
One bounded provider request per eligible row, no nested HTTP retry, per-row error classification and ten-minute embed_after cooldown.
acceptance: Poison rows do not block later rows; crashed scan resumes next tick; hidden/deleted rows skip admission and drafts never enter provider inputs.
Delayed success/failure across edit/retag fails text_at guard; both updates require embedding still NULL; cooldown reset by writer works.
Changing selected model requires stopped worker, clearing every vector and restarting with matched query/document config; no mixed model vectors.
verification: Oban uniqueness/crash tests, alternating50-row fairness fixture, stale-response race and model-switch maintenance rehearsal in isolated DB.
ownership: Search embedding scan worker; provider adapter; worker tests
sizing: One bounded embedding scan with row freshness and fairness. Reuse the selected provider; request search and global operational rescue remain separate.

title: Bound complete search work and keyword fallback
outcome: Each search request completes or returns retryable error within one measured budget under provider congestion.
scope: Choose explicit numeric shared provider concurrency, queue wait, per-call and total operation deadlines using P4b.01 measurements; keep request DB statement timeout2s.
Normalize/reject blank and oversized input before provider work; fallback omits vector branches within remaining overall budget and preserves filters/pagination.
acceptance: Saturated reader requests and embedding scan share bounded provider capacity; queue wait consumes the same deadline and cancelled local tasks release local resources.
Embedding/hybrid failure falls back only with remaining budget; keyword failure/expired total budget returns error, never empty success.
Fallback is internally observable but no degraded-mode notice; no failure caching, frozen ranking or unbounded connection-pool assumption.
verification: Deterministic deadline/queue saturation tests plus measured integrated provider and SQL timing; configure chosen numbers and record rationale.
ownership: Search orchestration and provider capacity boundary; timing/saturation tests
sizing: One end-to-end search budget and fallback behavior. Reuse retrieval and shared provider limits; keep page lifecycle outside this task.

title: Render URL-driven initial search pages
outcome: SearchLive renders useful initial HTML and one truthful result page for the requested query/filter/page.
scope: Own SearchLive permanently; disconnected and first connected loads use the same bounded synchronous Content operation.
Render compact text summaries, source-labelled escaped excerpts, native filters, bounded Previous/Next and distinct empty/error outcomes; coordinate shared component reservation with P16/P9.

Expose summary viewer-vote/capability fields and reserve the shared row action interface for P10 integration. This early search task does not implement the later voting feature or show a successful action stub.
Consume P16.02-owned shared component interfaces; reserve any required shared-file change through its owner instead of creating parallel controls.
acceptance: Typing performs no retrieval; blank submission preserves URL/heading/results/page with validation feedback; unchanged intent performs no new search.
Submitted query and exact filters live in URL, query/filter change resets page1 and Clear filters keeps submitted query; invalid/out-of-window pages normalize consistently.

No thumbnails/player, total-result claim, automatic filter relaxation, cached extra page or out-of-filter suggestions. Voting interaction acceptance is owned by P10 and its integration into this shared row.
verification: Disconnected/connected LiveView tests, search URL/filter cases and browser focus/initial HTML check using P0 driver.
ownership: SearchLive and search templates; P16.02-owned summary/filter components consumed by reservation; page tests
sizing: One initial URL-driven search page consuming P16.02 components and existing retrieval. Async subsequent navigation is P4b.06 and voting is P10.

title: Make later search navigation cancel stale work safely
outcome: Later URL changes and Retry update only the requested page without stale rows, errors or duplicate work.
scope: One page-owned begin_results helper cancels prior named async work and starts new work using scalar values, never socket.
Distinguish first connected synchronous load; submit/filter only patch URL, explicit Retry reruns same requested location.
acceptance: Delayed old results/cancellation exits do not overwrite current heading, rows, filters/page or show false errors; framework stale-result suppression is verified at pinned version.
Failure retains requested URL and offers Retry without old rows under new page; Retry adds no nonce/history entry.
Back/reconnect restore URL-driven state and useful reading position without a Back detector/history store; unpublished input does not become submitted by filter change.
verification: Controlled delayed async/cancellation LiveView tests and real-browser Back/reconnect/focus/Retry journey.
ownership: SearchLive lifecycle helper and focused async/browser tests
sizing: One later-navigation async lifecycle with cancellation and truthful display. Reuse initial page/retrieval code; no independent browser-history subsystem.

title: Run real integrated hybrid-search acceptance
outcome: The search boundary passes the same relevance, capacity and user-journey checks on its selected real runtime.
scope: Run ten-query gate, real extensions/runtime, source excerpts, filter recall and total-budget saturation on one integrated revision.
Measure warm/cold latency, memory, long-document inference and throughput including admission/hydration; record limitations instead of borrowing historical timings.
acceptance: All previously declared numerical and relevance gate rules pass or milestone remains blocked; exactly one selected runtime/config matches document/query preparation.
Keyword nonmatches, stale retag vectors, current visibility, fallback and async navigation suites pass; real provider is exercised, not replaced by stub success.
verification: Redacted repeatable evaluation report with revision, versions, corpus and measured thresholds/results; browser journey and independent reviews.
ownership: Search gate runner/report; integrated search evidence
sizing: One integrated search gate using the existing ten-query fixture, provider and browser suites. Record failures and return repairs to their owners, rather than changing thresholds to pass.

title: Verify Stream and R2 provider contracts before lifecycle code
outcome: Provider evidence establishes enforceable upload size/privacy/deadlines and trustworthy completion facts.
scope: Use feature-specific credentials and nonsecret configuration from P13a.01 in an isolated probe using P0.02 dependencies. This probe does not require a deployed release or unrelated providers. Final integration uses P13a.02 runtime configuration at the feature gate.
Probe pinned real Stream tus API for every video size, validated Upload-Length up to1GB, maxDurationSeconds180, requiresignedurls, fixed one-hour expiry and stream-media-id.
Verify uploaded timestamp represents completed direct upload rather than readiness/observation; verify signed iframe/poster, R2 put/delete/cache purge semantics.
Choose bounded provider timeouts/concurrency and parser selection with pinned version and demonstrated resource bounds; track fixture assets/cleanup.
acceptance: Browser-only size checks are insufficient; demonstrate server-authorized length cannot exceed1,000,000,000 bytes or report a blocking contract gap.
Private-from-reservation assets reject unsigned playback; actual completion timestamp supports completion+48h without extending late transfers.
Secrets never appear in evidence; unsupported semantics block gate and route to technical review, not silent architecture substitution.
A pinned maintained parser is selected by supported-format, trusted motion-classification and resource-bound fixtures before P5.02 starts.
verification: Redacted request/response trace, threshold/late-response provider experiments, signed URL check and fixture cleanup record.
ownership: Media provider probe fixtures/configuration; no production lifecycle implementation
sizing: One isolated provider capability and parser-selection probe, with recorded unresolved blockers. No production lifecycle state machine or release setup is implemented here.

title: Validate and store one recoverable image attempt
outcome: Content receives trusted files and attempt-scoped R2 identities while page-owned upload entries remain recoverable.
scope: The pinned bounded parser selected and proven in P5.01 validates PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF and trusted GIF/WebP/APNG motion; normalize optional description and generate media/UUID extension keys with trusted content type.
Enforce10MB each and50MB newly uploaded total; retained files excluded from byte allowance, final combined selection limited10.
Return explicit attempt results for content transaction/cleanup; no socket/temp-path background work or reusable page-only R2 staging.
acceptance: Malformed/unclassifiable/oversized input fails before unsafe storage and preserves submitted identity; parser resource ceiling is tested.
Later-file failure cleans only known unattached new objects; uncertain content commit never triggers blind deletion; retry creates fresh keys.
R2 key/content type derives from validated file, not client name; unchanged retained files are not reuploaded.
verification: Parser/type/motion/size boundary fixtures, deterministic later-put failure and unknown-outcome tests, real R2 put/get/delete round trip.
ownership: Media image validator/R2 attempt functions; parser/provider tests
sizing: One validated image-attempt boundary from page-owned paths to trusted R2 results. Reuse the chosen parser; browser entry management, durable cleanup and orphan sweep remain separate tasks.

title: Provision private video reservations with guarded identity
outcome: Authorized authors receive an upload endpoint only after its stable media identity and provider uid are durably safe.
scope: Implement begin_video_upload with server-owned target encoding, scope/target checks, shared limits and existing-publication reconciliation.
Persist row before one non-retried provisioning call; lock and persist uid only while NULL, uploading, noncleanup and before original deadline at wall time, then release URL.
acceptance: Client target/uid/other-account ids cannot claim access; new review requires live parent, edit requires eligible owner and original deleted content rejects.
Lost/late provisioning response, expiry lock wait and definite failure never release stale URL or revive a row; no provider discovery for NULL uid.
No content/vote/notification/search side effect occurs on selection; provider call is outside locks and privacy/duration/expiry metadata is server-owned.
verification: Reservation state/race tests and real tus authorization trace with committed uid-before-release evidence.
ownership: Media reservation/target encoder; Stream adapter; preflight contract tests
sizing: One private reservation/uid-publication invariant. Reuse admission and limits; transfer UI, status refresh and attachment claims are separate tasks.

title: Refresh video state through guarded bounded transitions
outcome: Authorized status reads make progress without mistaking uncertainty for failure or resurrecting assets.
scope: Implement bounded get_video_uploads inputs, per-id target/ownership admission and shared editor/expiry transition function.
Use trusted uploaded completion once, original1h eligibility, completion+48h recovery and playable duration<=180; use five-second provider call timeout initially and chosen small concurrency.
acceptance: Timeout/429 preserves committed facts, no ready regression; ready rows require no provider request, late results cannot affect attached/cleanup/deleted/replaced rows.
Observation/readiness time does not reset completion; late completion gets no recovery window; attach clears expiry/cooldown and later response cannot restore either.
Unowned/malformed/overlarge id lists fail before calls; content is never automatically published and no global readiness scanner/webhook appears.
verification: Status transition matrix, out-of-order responses, readiness-outage fixture and bounded-concurrency timing tests; provider completion probe reused.
ownership: Media status transitions/provider reads; focused state/race tests
sizing: One guarded provider-status transition with bounded reads. Editor scheduling and video expiry selection remain separate consumers of this transition.

title: Claim ordered media atomically for content saves
outcome: Publication/edit can atomically attach only the exact owned intended media set without racing discard or expiry.
scope: Provide transaction participant locking media in consistent order and checking final mixed count/positions, ownership/readiness/target and deadline after lock waits.
Support immutable exact-publication target equivalence for recovered new-submission videos used by explicit edit; preserve ids/order/descriptions and no version rebinding.
acceptance: Attach versus cleanup/discard has one winner; duplicate selection, moved existing attachment, wrong author/kind/key/parent or expired/deleted original rejects all changes.
Exact same published item may claim its still-owned ready unexpired unattached asset; URL/key possession alone grants nothing.
Commit attaches once and clears expiry/cooldown; rollback preserves reusable staged video; independent expected edit-version check is never weakened.
verification: Transactional mixed-order/identity fixtures and multi-connection attach/expiry/discard races, including exact-target equivalence rejection matrix.
ownership: Media claim transaction helper; content integration contract fixtures
sizing: One atomic ordered-media claim participant, including exact original-publication equivalence. Final editor transactions and browser recovery remain P6/P8 work.

title: Expire staged uploads fairly without extending author deadlines
outcome: Bounded expiry work makes progress past uncertain rows and safely retires abandoned reservations.
scope: Minute-cadence active-unique Oban media expiry scan, max_attempts1, at most50 due rows, bounded per-call and total runtime.
NULL uid expires locally; known unfinished uid reconciles trusted completion; uncertain result sets guarded wall-time+10min reconcile_after while original expiry stays fixed.
acceptance: Fifty uncertain first rows do not starve later due rows on the next eligible scan; cooldown survives restart and clears on definitive progress/claim/cleanup.
Completed processing/ready/failed rows expire at completion+48h; NULL uid triggers neither lookup nor provider cleanup job.
Provider work occurs outside locks; guarded transition and cleanup insertion serialize with claims and ignore late responses.
verification: 51-plus-row fairness and restart fixture, bounded run/uniqueness tests and clock-boundary claim/expiry races.
ownership: Media expiry worker; due query; expiry concurrency fixtures
sizing: One bounded staged-video expiry scan and uncertain-row fairness rule. Reuse guarded transitions and cleanup insertion; no readiness scanner or generic scheduler.

title: Retain durable cleanup through provider failure and job pruning
outcome: Removed media becomes inaccessible immediately while provider deletion remains recoverable until confirmed.
scope: Removal/discard/expiry transaction sets cleanup_at, clears position/cooldown and inserts Oban cleanup for known provider identifiers; expose participant to P3/P11.
Implement idempotent R2 delete/purge and Stream delete outside transaction; preserve media row until all required cleanup confirms.
acceptance: Crash between business commit and job execution loses no cleanup intent; pruning terminal jobs after seven days leaves the provider id recoverable.
Duplicate, timeout, delete or purge failure preserves durable state for retry; late status or attachment claims cannot revive membership.
Unknown publication commit reconciles database references before explicit deletion; live page termination or draft discard alone authorizes no uncertain-object cleanup.
verification: Transactional enqueue/rollback, duplicate/lost-response/pruning tests; real provider delete/purge evidence. Orphan-age/reference sweep fixtures belong to P5.10.
ownership: Media cleanup worker/transaction participant; provider deletion tests
sizing: One durable explicit-removal cleanup mechanism and provider deletion lifecycle. Orphan image discovery/sweep belongs only to P5.10.

title: Authorize and sign fresh media watch and thumbnail routes
outcome: Stable Tips media paths provide fresh current authorization and short-lived private provider destinations.
scope: One Content access function backs GET /media/:id/watch and /thumbnail; choose configured host and documented iframe/poster server-side.
Sign locally JOSE/RS256 one-hour token with downloads disabled; private,no-store redirects and fail-closed configuration.
acceptance: Public live attachment works; staged owner and hidden authorized author/moderator access use fresh admission; expired/cleanup/deleted/unready or wrong target denies.
Independently live review under hidden/deleted tip remains accessible; missing/broken key never falls back to bare uid or arbitrary redirect host.
Long-open page obtains new signed destination on opening; app HTML/storage contains only Tips ids/paths, not persistent playback tokens; issued token lifetime tradeoff documented.
verification: Authorization matrix/controller header/JWT-claim tests and actual signed iframe/poster verification against Stream.
ownership: Media access/signing; two controller routes; access/provider tests
sizing: One shared authorized signing boundary for two representations. Reuse current admission/visibility; player UI and provider ingestion are out of scope.

title: Verify media foundation with real providers and durable failures
outcome: The provider/storage lifecycle is safe to integrate into editor journeys on the current authenticated application.
scope: Run real R2 and private Stream round trips plus lifecycle races, deadline/fairness tests, signing and durable cleanup evidence.
Select measured shared media/provider/account request limits and verify aggregate queue/runtime capacity with the operations owner; editor UI journeys remain P6/P7.
acceptance: All fixed limits/privacy and completion semantics are enforced; absent credentials/unproven byte cap or timestamp blocks gate.
Fifty uncertain-row fairness, late response, NULL uid, attach/expiry, prune/reconstruct and ready-during-status-outage cases pass with no P0/P1 review findings.
Test assets use distinct prefixes/ids and tracked cleanup; no real-provider substitute or unexecuted historical result counts as pass.
verification: Integrated provider/race test report with revision/configuration, measured capacity/deadlines and asset cleanup ledger; independent review evidence.
ownership: Media foundation integration runner/evidence; provider capacity verification
sizing: One integrated media-foundation verification session using existing lifecycle/provider fixtures. Full editor journeys remain P6/P7; failed behavior returns to the named owning issue.

title: Sweep orphaned image objects without racing active attempts
outcome: A bounded weekly recovery sweep removes old unreferenced image objects while preserving active or committed media.
scope: Implement a bounded weekly Oban maintenance sweep over R2 image objects older than one hour, with bounded provider listing/deletion work and explicit continuation on a later run when needed.
Recheck committed media references, including cleanup records, before deleting an eligible object; retain the existing provider deletion/cache-purge helpers.
Enforce and test that active upload/content attempts finish or stop below the one-hour grace. No reusable orphan-eligible page staging keys or second recovery queue are introduced.
acceptance: An old object with no media row is deleted safely; young objects and any referenced object remain, including hidden attachments and cleanup-marked media.
An uncertain publication result is not treated as permission to delete; sweep fixtures include committed references after lost acknowledgement and active attempts within the grace.
Provider list/delete timeout and repeated execution retain resumable bounded progress without blocking the maintenance queue or deleting unrelated namespaces.
Old abandoned attempt objects are eventually removed; identifiers, age source and namespace come from trusted provider/application metadata.
verification: Clock-controlled young/old/reference/cleanup-row fixtures; provider pagination/failure tests; real R2 orphan sweep against an isolated test prefix with cleanup evidence.
ownership: Media orphan-image maintenance worker; R2 sweep fixtures
sizing: One recovery sweep with age/reference/rate boundaries; explicit attachment removal and video expiry remain P5.07 and P5.06. Reuse provider deletion helpers rather than rebuilding them.
